clue.text: Angle of ray?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to angle is to ... with rod and line
second meaning: a ray is a kind of flat sea creature, an example of the answer, hence the question mark

explanation.walkthrough: In the surface 'Angle of ray' sounds like geometry or optics; the two words are separate senses, one a verb, one a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Angling is the sport of catching fish, and the ray is a cartilaginous fish related to sharks.

clue.text: Butter — try a taste to begin with

parts.note: to have a go is to try

indicators.note: says only the opening letter of taste is used

parts.note: first letter T

explanation.surface: Someone sampling butter is told to have a little taste first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Butter' looks like the dairy spread; here it is one who butts.
explanation.definitionFit: A billy goat is notorious for ramming with its horns, so it is a creature that butts, a butter.

clue.text: Lunatic in US embracing one extreme of confabulation: animals that don't exist

indicators.note: the clue word that signals this step
a lunatic arrangement is a crazy one, so the letters of in US are jumbled

parts.note: the letters being jumbled
an extreme of confabulation is C or N, so the phrase reads literally as 'C or N', giving CORN

explanation.surface: A madman in America weaves tall tales about imaginary beasts.
explanation.walkthrough: The trick is 'one extreme of confabulation': either end letter of the word, C or N, written out as C OR N. 'Lunatic' jumbles IN US to UNIS, which embraces CORN.
explanation.definitionFit: Unicorns are mythical horned horses, legendary creatures with no real existence.

clue.text: These could be major or minor climbs

definitions.text: These could be major or minor
definitions.meaning: first meaning: musical ... come in major and minor keys
second meaning: a verb meaning climbs

explanation.walkthrough: 'Major or minor climbs' reads as mountaineering of different sizes; 'major or minor' belongs with the music sense instead.
explanation.definitionFit: Musicians practise sequences of notes in major and minor modes, and to scale a wall is to clamber up it.

clue.text: Recalled old college servant painting on wall

indicators.note: called back, so in a down clue the pieces are read from the bottom up

parts.note: a serf was a feudal servant bound to the land

explanation.surface: A retired college servant is remembered for a mural he once painted.
explanation.definitionFit: A fresco is a mural made by applying pigment onto wet plaster on a wall or ceiling.

clue.text: Stone containers capsizing a cargo ship

indicators.note: a capsizing ship is overturned, so its letters are thrown into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Heavy stone crates are lost when a cargo vessel overturns.
explanation.definitionFit: Sarcophagi are stone coffins, often carved, used in ancient burials.

clue.text: Spill e.g. a toilet's contents in a smooth flow

indicators.note: what is held inside the words Spill e.g. a toilet's gives the answer

explanation.surface: An unpleasant instruction to empty a lavatory bowl steadily.
explanation.definitionFit: Legato is the musical direction for notes played smoothly and connected, without breaks.

clue.text: Police officer's personal cut

parts.note: DI is a Detective Inspector, plus the 's
something personal is your own

explanation.surface: A policeman's own share of the proceeds, his personal cut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cut' looks like a share of loot; it is the verb meaning to snub or reject someone.
explanation.definitionFit: To cut someone is to cut them off, refusing any further relationship, as a parent may disown a child.

clue.text: More than one body in hearse? Lawsuits follow

indicators.note: the lawsuits come after the hearse in the answer

parts.note: a hearse is a car for carrying coffins
lawsuits are court cases

explanation.surface: A funeral car carries several corpses, and litigation inevitably comes next.
explanation.definitionFit: Carcases, a variant spelling of carcasses, are dead bodies, usually of animals.

clue.text: These can detect shots outside a locked room

indicators.note: the shots go around the outside of the room

parts.note: photographs are shots
a prison cell is a locked room

explanation.surface: A detective-story device: gunshots heard outside a locked room.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Detect' and 'locked room' summon a mystery novel; here 'detect' just means sense light.
explanation.definitionFit: Photocells are light sensors, used for example to detect someone breaking a beam.

clue.text: Monster of Rowling's creation originally

indicators.note: the original or opening letters of each word are taken

explanation.surface: A beast dreamed up by J. K. Rowling, the Harry Potter author.
explanation.walkthrough: Rowling's name points to her fantasy creatures, though this one belongs more to Tolkien.
explanation.definitionFit: An orc is a brutish goblin-like creature of fantasy fiction.

clue.text: Bar code's heading scanned backwards to find fiddler?

indicators.note: read in the reverse direction, so the letters run back to front

parts.note: taken as written; that the reversed letters also run through Bar code's is a coincidence, as the C comes from the heading of code

indicators.note: the head, or first letter, of code is used

parts.note: first letter C

explanation.surface: A barcode is read the wrong way round to identify a violinist.
explanation.walkthrough: A fiddler crab is a small crab with one oversized claw; the question mark warns that 'fiddler' is an example, not a synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: The fiddler crab is named after the male's single enlarged claw, waved like a violin bow.

clue.text: Act out of character, curiously more mischievous

indicators.note: the letters of Act are taken out of the longer word
done in a curious, odd way, so the remaining letters are rearranged

parts.note: the word whose letters are used
the letters removed

explanation.surface: Behaving unusually, someone becomes oddly naughtier.
explanation.walkthrough: Take A, C and T out of CHARACTER to leave CHRAER, then 'curiously' rearranges those letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Arch means playfully knowing or roguish, so archer is the comparative, more roguish.

clue.text: Animal's orgasms regularly ignored

indicators.note: every other letter of orgasms is skipped, keeping the rest

explanation.surface: A cheeky line about a beast whose climaxes are routinely overlooked.
explanation.definitionFit: A ram is a male sheep, a common farm creature.

clue.text: Stout overlayer on inside of coat being the main attraction

parts.note: the frothy head lies on top of a glass of stout
a coat's lining is its inside layer

explanation.surface: A recipe-like jumble of beer froth and coat fabric.
explanation.walkthrough: Stout is a dark beer such as Guinness, whose creamy top is the head.
explanation.definitionFit: A performer headlining a show is the star act, top of the bill.

clue.text: Commanding officer in corrupt prison's a dangerous individual

indicators.note: the officer goes inside the rearranged letters
corrupt means spoiled or perverted, so the letters of prison are scrambled

parts.note: CO is the military abbreviation for Commanding Officer

explanation.surface: A commander inside a crooked jail is a menace.
explanation.definitionFit: A scorpion has a venomous sting, so the word suits a menacing person or creature.

clue.text: What triggers prompter's hint when line's forgotten

definitions.text: What triggers prompter's hint when line's forgotten

indicators.note: the line is left out, so its letter drops from the word

parts.note: a clue is a hint
L is the abbreviation for line

explanation.surface: In a theatre, the prompter whispers a hint when an actor dries.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines the answer too: when an actor forgets a line, the prompter gives one.
explanation.definitionFit: A cue is a signal prompting an actor's next line or action on stage.

clue.text: For example, open door by mechanism comprising key

parts.note: a means is a mechanism or method
made of, consisting of
Escape is a key on a computer keyboard

explanation.surface: Instructions for opening a door with a mechanism worked by a key.
explanation.definitionFit: An open door offers a way out, an exit route, the very thing the phrase describes.

clue.text: Idiot senior citizen at last turning up the volume

indicators.text: at last turning up the volume
indicators.note: the last letter, the musical soft sign, is swapped for the loud sign

parts.note: OAP is an old-age pensioner

explanation.surface: An elderly person finally cranks the sound up and seems foolish.
explanation.walkthrough: In music P (piano) means soft and F (forte) means loud, so turning up the volume changes P to F. OAP is the British abbreviation for an old-age pensioner.
explanation.definitionFit: An oaf is a clumsy, stupid lout.

clue.text: A little problem reported with stove pipe?

indicators.note: spoken out loud, so a word sounding like the problem is used

parts.note: a sum is an arithmetic problem
a stovepipe is a tall hat, so the question mark marks an example

explanation.surface: A minor issue mentioned with a chimney flue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stove pipe' looks like plumbing; here it is the tall top hat worn by Abraham Lincoln.
explanation.definitionFit: Somewhat means to some degree, slightly, rather.

clue.text: Study, as I said

indicators.note: spoken aloud, the pronoun sounds like the answer

parts.note: the word I, the first-person pronoun

explanation.surface: Someone repeating themselves while asking another to look closely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'As I said' seems to be a conversational aside; it signals that the answer sounds like I.
explanation.definitionFit: To eye something is to look at it closely, to study it.

clue.text: Start of play in which cow gets away

parts.note: to cow someone is to bully them
gone off is gone away

explanation.surface: A game in which a cow escapes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cow' looks like the animal, a female, but it is the verb meaning intimidate. A bully-off is the old way of starting a hockey game.
explanation.definitionFit: In field hockey the bully-off was the face-off that began play, two players clashing sticks.

clue.text: Ideal location of youth centre, excellent viewed both ways

indicators.note: the central letter of youth is taken

parts.note: middle letter U
top means excellent, first-rate; A1 also means excellent

indicators.note: excellent is read once forwards and once backwards, so the second reading runs in reverse

explanation.surface: Where the young congregate is outstanding from every angle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Excellent' does double duty: TOP read normally, then A1 (first-class) read backwards as IA, the 1 standing for the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: Utopia is Thomas More's imagined perfect society, now any ideal place.

clue.text: Think incessantly, turning over actresses' bombshell revelation

indicators.note: turned upside down in a down clue, so the letters read in reverse
revealed within the words actresses' bombshell

explanation.surface: Brooding endlessly over a shocking disclosure by actresses.
explanation.definitionFit: To obsess is to dwell constantly on one thing, unable to stop thinking about it.

clue.text: Fluffy, vacuously frilly with internal deficit

indicators.note: the deficit is placed inside
emptied out, so only the outer letters of frilly remain

parts.note: outer letters F and Y
a deficit is a loss

explanation.surface: Describing something fluffy and frilly yet hollow inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Flossy means soft and downy like floss silk, hence fluffy.

clue.text: Infuriate First Daughter ousted by independent young woman

indicators.note: says it is the earlier of the two daughter letters in the word that goes
pushed out and replaced by

parts.note: to madden is to infuriate

explanation.surface: A president's daughter loses her place to an independent young woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First Daughter' suggests a president's child; it means the first D in the word.
explanation.definitionFit: A maiden is an archaic or poetic word for a girl or unmarried woman.

clue.text: Don't set aside one point to make another

definitions.note: here another point, the answer being a small point or spot

indicators.note: put to one side, so removed from the word

parts.note: N, north, is one point of the compass

explanation.surface: Advice not to drop one argument just to make a different one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Point' looks like an argument; the first is a compass point and the second, 'another', is a small mark.
explanation.definitionFit: A dot is a tiny point, like a full stop.

clue.text: We don't approve of this new benefit

parts.note: boo is the cry of disapproval

explanation.surface: Critics of a new welfare benefit voice their disapproval.
explanation.definitionFit: A boon is a blessing or advantage, something helpful.

clue.text: Check publisher of online talks, without humour and dull

indicators.note: outside, so the first pieces surround the humour

parts.note: to check is to slow down
TED publishes its talks online
wit is humour

explanation.surface: A dismissal of a lecture website's talks as humourless and boring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' looks like 'lacking'; here it has its old sense of outside.
explanation.definitionFit: Slow-witted means mentally sluggish or stupid, one sense of dull.

clue.text: Double time and finish in front

parts.note: to win is to finish ahead of the rest

explanation.surface: A race report: double time and a winning finish.
explanation.definitionFit: A twin or double is an exact counterpart or lookalike.

clue.text: Drain with no cover that carries water

definitions.note: describes a vessel; the answer is a noun naming it

indicators.note: in a down clue the top letter is the cover, so it is removed

parts.note: a sewer is a drain

explanation.surface: An open drain conveying water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'That carries water' seems to describe the drain; it defines a large jug.
explanation.definitionFit: A ewer is a wide-mouthed jug or pitcher, traditionally for washing water.

clue.text: Adulates with unseemly oiliness

indicators.note: improper or disorderly, so the letters of oiliness are rearranged

explanation.surface: Fawning over someone with a slimy, improper sycophancy.
explanation.definitionFit: To lionise is to treat someone as a celebrity, a form of hero-worship.

clue.text: Remarks directed to audience for the better songs

definitions.meaning: first meaning: stage remarks only the audience hears
second meaning: A-sides are the lead tracks of singles

explanation.walkthrough: On a vinyl single the A-side carried the intended hit and the B-side the lesser song.
explanation.definitionFit: Actors deliver asides in theatre, while A-sides were the featured tracks on records.
